figures.alt: Localized split seal at a skylight flashing corner on a shingle roof
figures.caption: A roof patch begins with tracing the entry point, not with the ceiling stain. Flashing, penetrations, roof covering, and the attic side of the assembly all need inspection before a permanent repair is selected.
figures.before: When You Need a Permit in Jacksonville

figures.alt: Plumbing vent passing through shingles with a clean black pipe boot and flashing flange
figures.caption: Roof penetrations are common leak paths because they interrupt the shingle field. A temporary cover may control immediate water, but the permanent repair must restore the layered water-shedding sequence.

figures.alt: Roof drip edge and underlayment layered correctly at a shingle eave
figures.caption: After the repair, inspect from the attic during the next rain and look beyond the original stain. Lifted shingles, wet insulation, or new staining can point to a larger water path than one surface patch.
